note: The bands the E-flite Pitts S-1S 850mm plant has to land in, from docs/PITTS-STAGE1.md, which derives each from E-flite's published figures, its photographs, APC's data for the 11 x 7E, the BL15's class of motor, Prandtl's and Munk's biplane theory and the full size S-1S's published roll rate (scripts/pitts-derive.js prints the derived figures). E-flite publishes no bench or flight figure, so the performance bands are about derived figures built on an ESTIMATED motor and drag. Never widened to pass; argue in the derivation instead.

p1_level_75.source: level speed at three quarter throttle, the trim, derived 13.33 on the estimated thrust line and the biplane's polar; the Edge's 15 percent either side

p2_stall.source: sqrt(2W / rho S CLmax_cell), derived 9.78 at E-flite's 1529 g on 28.2 dm^2 with the cell's CLmax 0.908, where the top wing reaches each wing's 0.90 (CLmax / bip_r top); alphaStall is where the top wing stalls, 0.90 / (0.9911 x 4.1895), 12.42 deg; the Kadet's band in proportion, 0.94 to 1.14 of the formula, since the plant reads the stall at the blend's midpoint

p3_glide.source: L/D at 1.4 Vs, 13.69 m/s, derived 5.83 on the biplane's induced drag (a monoplane of the same span and area would glide at 5.36); 11 percent either side, the Edge's

p4_top.source: level speed at full throttle on 3S, derived 18.84, 10 percent either side

p5_roll.source: full aileron on E-flite's high rate, 18 mm of all four ailerons at 48 mm of chord, 22 deg through the surface's knee, from level at 15 m/s: the helix angle Clda da / -Clp on both wings in each other's wash, derived 0.204 (412 deg/s at 15 m/s), 20 percent either side; and at least the full size four aileron S-1S's 'around 220' deg/s (Budd Davisson, airbum.com), whose own pb/2V at its 120 mph cruise is 0.188

p5_low.source: the same on E-flite's low rate, 12 mm, 14.5 deg: derived 0.151, 20 percent either side

p6_pitch.source: 0.15 of up stick at once from level at the trim, 3.0 deg of elevator through the expo and the knee, which asks 10.2 deg of alpha, short of the stall blend's 10.4: the time to the pitch rate's first peak on the linear longitudinal model, derived 0.212 s to 24 deg/s; the Edge's band, 35 percent under and 50 over. A larger step is past the stall: half stick asks 18.6 deg, full 30.5

p8_inverted.source: the same symmetric section on both wings at one incidence: 'The S-1S doesn't know right side up from upside down and doesn't care' (Davisson): on its back at three quarter throttle it flies within 5 percent of its upright speed, stalls within 6 percent of its upright stall speed and rolls within 5 percent of its upright rate, the Edge's bands for the same claim

p9_snap.source: the edge of the envelope, from level at the trim with the ailerons centred. A yank alone, full up at once, asks 30.5 deg of alpha against the top wing's 12.4: 'Stalls were comfortable and easy to recover from' (Greg Gimlick, Park Pilot, spring 2019, of this kit), so it stalls, turns less than a quarter turn in 1.2 s and stops within 0.5 s of letting go, AOPA's recovery time below (the first run of this gate took the Edge's 0.3 s, which has no source, and read 0.35). The snap roll is AOPA's ('Technique: Snap rolls', Flight Training, September 2014, 'a power-on spin': 'pull back hard on the stick' and 'add a strong yawing motion with rudder in the desired direction', entered 'straight and level at a normal airspeed'), inside ('snaps inside and out', the same review; the outside snap is recorded, not banded, docs/PITTS-STAGE1.md says why): held 2 s it autorotates the rudder's way, still turning at half its peak rate or more over the last half second, at least a quarter turn, and AOPA's recovery, 'rudder opposite the direction of the turn, and reduce back-pressure', stops it within 0.5 s. No source gives an RC or full size snap's rate; the doc sets the plant's against Knight and Wenzinger's stable autorotation of a biplane cell (NACA TR 379)

p10_prop_torque.source: static full throttle, rolling left: APC's 11 x 7E torque at the derived 8,344 rpm, 0.276 N m, 25 percent either side

p11_rest.source: the drawn model at rest off E-flite's side photograph, 12.30 deg nose up, the CG 0.2134 m up, 19.7 percent of the weight on the tailwheel; half a degree, 5 mm and 3.5 points either way

p12_takeoff.source: the throttle opened over a second on grass, the tail up, rotated at 1.2 Vs to 10 deg at the pitch rate the pilot's stick gives: derived liftoff 13.36 m at 12.19 m/s in 2.6 s on a thrust little over the weight; the distance band the Cub's in proportion, 27 percent under and 45 over, the speed 15 percent either side

p13_straight.source: the same take off with the pilot's feet on the rudder and the tailwheel it steers: E-flite's 'steer with the rudder'

p14_taxi.source: full right rudder at walking pace, the throttle whose static thrust is 1.3 times the rolling resistance on grass, the Edge's taxi (0.31, pitts:derive): the 0.573 m wheelbase over tan of the tailwheel's half of the rudder, derived 2.58 m, the Edge's band in proportion, 21 percent under and 32 over. The shortest turn of any taildragger here: the short coupling

p15_landing.source: a powered approach, a flare and the tail held down, E-flite's 'hold full up elevator after touchdown': at rest on three wheels at P11's attitude, no hull or prop

b1_induced.source: the induced drag factor the plant flies, dCD / d(CL^2) between level at the trim and level at full throttle: Prandtl's biplane form on the lift each wing carries, derived 0.1143 (Munk's span factor 1.131, e 0.85), 5 percent either side; a monoplane of the same span and area, 0.1462, is outside it

b2_linear.source: short of either wing's stall the two wings' lifts sum to the cell's table lift, cl_alpha alpha plus the elevator's cl_de delta_e, within half a percent

b3_top_first.source: a slow pull into the stall, upright and on its back: the top wing, ahead and in the bottom wing's bound vortex upwash, carries more lift for its area and falls short of its linear lift first, and the bottom wing, washed down less by a stalled top wing, gains over its own; 'use different airfoil sections top and bottom to make the top wing stall first whether inverted or right side up' (Davisson, of the factory S-1S; E-flite's foam wings share one section, so here it is the stagger's upwash alone)

b4_unmoved.source: every other aircraft's recorded flight hash in Node, as extra:gates E15 stores them and the Extra's own E16, all from main's module at 71c0cbc, before the Pitts and its second wing existed

b5_cross_host.source: the Pitts's recorded take off, roll, snap and recovery, state trace hash, Node against headless Chrome
